title: Marks, Probes, Graphemes, Ranges & Moods
description: Seeded strokes that boil, a CSS collision probe, grapheme-safe splitting, UI anchored inside an input, and a face made of six numbers.

drops.title: Every Mark Is a Function
drops.description: Hand-drawn strokes generated from a seed, re-rolled eight times a second to get the boil of real animation.
drops.concept: Nothing in the drawing is stored — each stroke is a function of a seeded random number generator: the wobble along its length, the overshoot past the corner, the pressure taper and the second pass that never quite retraces the first. The same seed reproduces the same picture anywhere, so advancing the seed on a three-frame cycle produces boil, the twitch that makes hand-drawn animation read as hand-drawn. Three styles change the mark itself: ballpoint cross-hatch, crayon scumble, and a single confident ink line over an offset wash.
drops.source: alexgreensh/anidoodle — hand-drawn art and animation, written as code

interaction.mouse: Sliders change wobble, passes, overshoot and the boil rate.
interaction.click: Switch mark style, or re-roll the seed for a different hand.
interaction.touch: Everything is sliders and buttons; the panel stacks above the sheet.

drops.title: Overlap, Detected
drops.description: An anchored strip with a fixed-width child inside it turns scrollable the moment two elements close in on each other.
drops.concept: CSS has no collision query, so this builds one: anchor positioning stretches an invisible probe from the right edge of a decoration to the left edge of the content, and a fixed-width pseudo-element sits inside it. Once the gap shrinks below that width the probe overflows, its scroll timeline activates a 1ms animation that sets a custom property, and a style container query reads the flag. Three panels respond differently to the same signal.
drops.source: Ahmad Shadeed — “Detect when elements overlap with CSS” (Sep 2026)

interaction.mouse: Drag each panel's width slider until the card closes in on the ornament.
interaction.click: Toggle “show the probe strip” to see the measured gap itself.
interaction.touch: Sliders and the live gap readout work the same on touch.

drops.title: Split It Properly
drops.description: Per-letter animation breaks emoji, Devanagari and Thai — Intl.Segmenter splits text the way a reader does.
drops.concept: Every stagger effect starts by splitting a string, and almost all of them use [...text], which tears a four-person family emoji into seven code points, strands Devanagari vowel signs and detaches combining accents. Intl.Segmenter has shipped everywhere since 2024 and splits by grapheme, by word — including Japanese and Thai, which have no spaces — and by sentence, where split('.') never sees a question mark and cuts decimals in half.

interaction.mouse: Flip each demo between the naive splitter and the segmenter and watch the counts change.
interaction.click: Cycle specimen strings and switch language for the word demo.
interaction.touch: Buttons only; the sentence highlighter advances on its own.

drops.title: Inside the Input
drops.description: A popover anchored to the token being typed, a squiggle under one substring, and a picker at the caret — inside real form fields.
drops.concept: An input has always been a black box: you can read the value but not ask where its third word sits on screen. Edge's new OpaqueRange hands you live ranges inside form fields with getBoundingClientRect(), which is what mention menus, inline spelling marks and caret-anchored pickers have always needed. Until it ships everywhere the shim is a hidden mirror element carrying the field's own metrics — both paths are wired here, and a toggle forces the shim so you can compare.

interaction.mouse: Type @ for the mention menu, edit the typo line, or type : in the textarea.
interaction.click: Pick from either popover to insert at the right offset.
interaction.touch: All three fields are real inputs — the on-screen keyboard works normally.

drops.title: One Ball, Thirty Moods
drops.description: An assistant avatar with no sprite sheet — an expression is six numbers, spring-interpolated between moods.
drops.concept: The status spinner is being replaced by a face, and this one is pure geometry: lid opening, eye curve, brow angle, mouth bend, mouth opening and body squash. Changing mood springs those six numbers to new targets while the blink loop, idle bob and pointer tracking keep running underneath, so transitions are never cut off. Ten moods, a scripted agent sequence, and the same component legible at 44px and 26px.
drops.source: sam70361/aora-bot — Emotion Ball, a pure-SVG expression engine

interaction.mouse: Eyes track the pointer; stiffness, damping and blink rate are tunable.
interaction.click: Pick any of the ten moods, or run the scripted agent sequence.
interaction.touch: Mood chips work on tap; pointer tracking idles to centre.
